positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Performed modification to a genetic algorithm program for my research at University of Southern California.  The program was written in C# and its purpose was to performed evaluations on design, cost, and energy efficiency for building profiles in Autodesk Revit.  Each building's profile was stored in an excel sheet and was the input for all of the calculations.  My team planned the modifications to expand the functionality of the program after examining and understanding the code, its interaction with the Autodesk Revit software, and the connection to the Green Building Studio (GBS) database.  We used what we learned to decide on the best way to redesign the code for our goal of modifying the program for evaluating multiple buildings at a time, decreasing the run-time, and increasing efficiency.  Our implementation involved running multiple buildings at a time, replacing the user interface with automated control for a decreased run-time, and applying a scripting program with AutoHotKey to overlay the entire execution of the program.  Due to bugs in the program, our constant support for the application was dire.  For example, while trying to implement evaluations for multiple buildings at one time, I was required to implement a lock on the GBS connection between requests from different building, which prevented multiple buildings accessing the same resources at once.  Integrating AutoHotKey into the interface was another key solution in decreasing run-time and increasing efficiency of the evaluation process which led to faster results.

Software Utilized: 

MATLAB, Python, C#, Visual Studio, AutoHotKey, Autodesk Revit, Green Building Studio, and Microsoft Excel

positions.title: Department of Homeland Security Reseach Team
positions.description:
Performed research in the computer science field at CSUDH.  My first project was developing, testing, and launching an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) for search and survey.  I lead a team of researchers in developing software for operating the vehicle, designing models of the AUV, and simulating the model in a 3D virtual environment.  Models were created in X3D, simulations were performed in the AUV workbench.  Other languages used were Java and XML.

Software Utilized: AUV Workbench, X3D Viewer, Visual Studio

My second project was a collaborative  Word Frequency Entity Correlation Data Visualization Application (WoFECs DVA), which utilized geotag data from global RSS feeds to plot the frequency of that data over a period of time in correlation with geographic locations.  By showing the frequency of certain words in the data plot, global threats could be predicted, therefore aiding in the security of global defense.  I developed WoFECs DVA using Java and a free library called JFreeChart.

Software Utilized: NetBeans, Java, MySQL, JFreeChart Java library
